key_insight: The paper shows that fault-tolerant quantum computers can simulate atomic nuclei using adapted shell-model and no-core-shell-model Hamiltonians, but the cost varies sharply by nuclear model and system size.
engineering_relevance: It provides the first fault-tolerant resource estimates for nuclear simulation, helping engineers judge when quantum advantage may be realistic versus when bespoke algorithms will be needed.
method: Compile quantum algorithms for effective shell-model Hamiltonians.
Extend the approach to no-core-shell-model Hamiltonians with three-body chiral EFT interactions.
Estimate Toffoli gate and qubit counts for representative nuclei such as 32Mg, 219At, and light nuclei up to 40Ca.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports resource estimates showing shell-model cases can be comparable to recent chemistry benchmarks, while no-core-shell-model cases are much more expensive.
watch_item: No-core-shell-model simulations for light nuclei appear prohibitively costly with current methods, so practical deployment likely requires new, problem-specific optimizations.
paper_title: Fault-tolerant quantum algorithms for simulating atomic nuclei
